articles.headline: Drake Maye: Patriots offense, own play 'unacceptable'
articles.description: Drake Maye, whose early-season struggles continued with two interceptions and a lost fumble in Sunday's 35-6 blowout loss to the Jaguars, called the offense's performance "unacceptable" as he looks within himself for answers.
articles.body:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- Patriots quarterback Drake Maye, whose early-season struggles continued with two interceptions and a lost fumble in Sunday's 35-6 blowout loss to the Jaguars, called the offense's performance "unacceptable" as he looks within himself for answers.

"It's disappointing. The ball starts rolling that way, we can't get out of our own way, and I can't get out of my own way personally -- I have to look myself in the mirror and take this as a turning point," he said.

"It's Week 3, and at the same time we have to have some fuel and realize that what we're doing out there offensively it's unacceptable. It's been unacceptable for three weeks. I have to start with myself, lead these guys, and get back after it."

Last year's MVP runner-up, Maye finished 14-of-25 passing for 199 yards, with no touchdowns and an 11.9 Total QBR, the lowest by a Patriots starter since Bailey Zappe (1.9) in Week 18 of the 2023 season against the New York Jets.

His six interceptions overall are the most by a Patriots quarterback through three games of a season since Drew Bledsoe had six in 1994.

"We haven't made good decisions with the football. We have to get it fixed," coach Mike Vrabel said after his team slipped to 1-2. "And everybody else has to do much better, starting with me."

In Sunday's loss, in which Maye was pressured on 11 dropbacks in the first half (career high for a half, per ESPN Research), the turnover issues began late in the first quarter when the football slipped out of his hand while attempting a pass with the Jaguars recovering. Maye said after the game that center Jared Wilson had been bleeding on his hand, which led to it slipping on his pass attempt to receiver Kyle Williams.

"At the same time, I have to hold on to the football," he said.

Then in position to slice into the Jaguars' 14-3 lead late in the second quarter, Maye threw an ill-advised pass on third-and-goal from the 2 looking for receiver Efton Chism III along the end line that cornerback Travis Hunter picked off for his first career interception.

"Just forcing it," Maye said, which continued an issue that began in the fourth quarter of a season-opening loss to the Seahawks when he threw three fourth-quarter interceptions.

Maye fired a third-quarter pick on a comeback route to Williams that he said he shouldn't have attempted.

After the game, Maye was asked if the right shoulder injury that led to him taking a pain-killing injection before Super Bowl LX in February has lingered at all early this season.

"I like to say that when you have that much time off and you get to focus on getting back, you're going out there healthy," said Maye, who previously noted the injury didn't require surgery.

"You're going to get banged up every now and then but at the same time, a lot of guys are banged up. I'm looking forward to getting back to playing winning football, that's the main thing. And knowing I play a big role in that and taking the bull by its horns ... I wouldn't sa

articles.headline: NFL Week 3: Takeaways, questions, fantasy spin for Sunday's games
articles.description: Our NFL Nation reporters react to all the action, answering the biggest questions coming out of each Sunday game. Here's what we learned from Week 3.
articles.body:
Week 3 of the 2026 NFL season featured shocking performances in the early window Sunday, including another  turnover-filled afternoon by Patriots quarterback Drake Maye and a three-touchdown performance by Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs. Commanders backup quarterback Marcus Mariota also led the team to a huge upset over the Seahawks.

Elsewhere during the early window, the Steelers got the best of a shootout versus the Bengals. The Giants defeated the Titans without starting quarterback Jaxson Dart, and the Browns won their second straight game.

Our NFL Nation reporters reacted to all the action, answering lingering questions coming out of each game and detailing everything else you need to know for teams that played Sunday. Fantasy football analysts Matt Bowen and Tristan Cockcroft also have fantasy takeaways from each matchup. Let's get to it.

TEN-NYG | LAC-BUF | HOU-IND

NYJ-DET | NE-JAX | KC-MIA

ATL-GB

Washington 33, Seattle 31

Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Commanders

How did this happen? Turnovers and an efficient offense. The Commanders forced three turnovers, leading to three touchdowns -- two by the offense and another on a pick-six by linebacker Kain Medrano. The offense capitalized on two short fields after a fumble and an interception, while quarterback Marcus Mariota did what was needed. He was smart with the ball, making quick throws and taking checkdowns to keep the chains moving. And he was aggressive when necessary, like on a tight-window throw to WR Trey Burks for his second touchdown. It was an unlikely win without quarterback Jayden Daniels, linebacker Frankie Luvu, tight end Chig Okonkwo, right guard Sam Cosmi and safety Nick Cross.

Trend to watch: Washington did not force any turnovers in its first two games, which continued an ugly trend: Only one team has forced fewer turnovers than the Commanders since 2024. But they harped on it all offseason, and the focus paid off Sunday. Can they sustain it? It helped that they played coverage much better than they did against Dallas in Week 2. But to get more, the front needs to generate more consistent pressure. It'll help when they get blitzing linebacker Frankie Luvu back soon from a groin injury. -- John Keim

Next game: vs. Colts in London (Sunday, 9:30 a.m. (London) p.m. ET)

Seahawks

What was most concerning about Seattle's upset loss? The defending Super Bowl champions came into this game on a 12-game winning streak, with Sam Darnold back at quarterback, and as the much healthier team. There were plenty of reasons they lost as 8.5-point favorites, but a big one was their absence of a run game -- something they could have used in the rain. articles.headline: Buccaneers WR Jalen McMillan suffers knee injury vs. Vikings
articles.description: Buccaneers wide receiver Jalen McMillan suffered a knee injury in the first quarter against the Vikings and has been ruled out.
articles.body:
TAMPA, Fla. -- Tampa Bay Buccaneers wide receiver Jalen McMillan suffered a knee injury in the first quarter against the Minnesota Vikings and has been ruled out.

It is the same knee that McMillan injured during training camp that forced him to miss multiple weeks and the season opener. He returned to game action last week in a limited capacity but was expected to play a bigger role this week as the Bucs attempt to climb out of an 0-2 hole for the first time since 2014.

McMillan suffered the injury colliding with Vikings safety Josh Metellus while attempting to catch a pass on a corner route.

It is unclear whether McMillan suffered the injury while pivoting his body or upon contact. He was able to limp off the field under his own power.

articles.headline: Parma part ways with ex-Arsenal assistant Carlos Cuesta
articles.description: Parma parted ways with coach Carlos Cuesta on Sunday after winning only one of their opening five Serie A matches.
articles.headlineJa: パルマ、元アーセナル助監督のカルロス・クエスタ氏と契約解除
articles.descriptionJa: パルマはセリエA開幕5試合でわずか1勝にとどまり、日曜日にカルロス・クエスタ監督と解任・退任の道を歩むこととなった。
articles.body:
Parma parted ways with coach Carlos Cuesta on Sunday after winning only one of their opening five Serie A matches.

The club said Cuesta "has been relieved of his duty" and that "following an internal discussion between the club and coach, it was agreed that the conditions in order to continue this working relationship and the advancement of the sporting project, were not being met. Both parties came to a mutual agreement."

- Goals galore! Why Barça's start to season is best in Europe's top leagues for almost 100 years

- Udinese sign former Real Madrid defender Alaba

- Havertz back at Arsenal for injury treatment

A replacement was not immediately named.

Parma beat Genoa last weekend but only have four points.

Cuesta became the youngest manager in Europe's top five leagues, and the youngest Serie A manager in almost a century, when he was appointed by Parma in June 2025 at the age of 29. He had previously spent five years as assistant to Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta.

Having decided at a young age that his future lay in coaching rather than playing, Cuesta was given his first chance at Atlético Madrid with their underage teams and after four years there, went travelling Europe to study coaching methods.

It was during this period that Cuesta met Arteta, then part of Pep Guardiola's coaching staff at Manchester City, and after a two-year spell with Juventus' youth academy, Cuesta joined Arsenal in 2020.

He guided Parma to a 13th-place finish last season.

It's the third coaching change in Serie A this season after Paolo Vanoli replaced Fabio Grosso at Fiorentina and Raffaele Palladino replaced Domenico Tedesco at Bologna.

Parma's next match is at Serie A champions Inter Milan on Oct. 10 after the international break.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.headline: LaLiga chief Javier Tebas criticises Man City's alleged rule breaches: 'Equal rules for all'
articles.description: LaLiga president Javier Tebas has said Manchester City legal battle against the Premier League shows why "equal rules for all" are essential.
articles.headlineJa: ラ・リーガのテバス会長、マンCのルール違反疑惑を批判：「すべての人に平等なルールを」
articles.descriptionJa: ラ・リーガのハビエル・テバス会長は、マンチェスター・シティのプレミアリーグに対する法的闘争が、なぜ「すべての人に平等なルール」が不可欠であるかを示していると語った。
articles.body:
LaLiga president Javier Tebas has said Manchester City legal battle against the Premier League shows why "equal rules for all" are essential to protect football's integrity and sustainability.

ESPN reported on Friday that a source has confirmed City are expected to be found guilty on the vast majority of charges of financial breaches in their legal case with the Premier League.

In a statement, City didn't deny the guilty verdicts and said that the process "remains ongoing."

When contacted by ESPN on Friday, the Premier League said it wouldn't comment on a "private and confidential process."

The Athletic first reported Friday that City had been found guilty of all but one of the 115 charges by an independent panel.

- Ogden: Man City verdict will leave a stain and stench on a Premier League era

In 2020, Man City succeeded in overturning a two-year European competition ban from UEFA at the Court of Arbitration, after being found to have breached the governing body's Financial Fair Play (FFP) rule.

Tebas had previously spoken out against "so-called financial doping in European football".

In a lengthy post on X, Tebas reflected on those statements he had given during the Soccerex event, which had been held in Manchester during September 2017.

Tebas also called the CAS ruling a "deeply misguided decision" which was "extraordinarily damaging to the credibility of European football's economic control system" and again stressed the same rules must apply to all clubs.

"Economic sustainability is not bureaucracy. Financial control is not a whim," he said.

"And arguing that clubs should compete fundamentally with the resources they are able to generate doesn't mean being against any specific club either. It's about defending a model.

"A model in which sporting success doesn't depend on who has the most powerful financial backing behind them, but on who manages best, generates more resources, builds better teams, and respects the same rules as everyone else.

"Defending this position has cost me a lot of criticism and not a few headaches. But I still think exactly the same as I did in Manchester in 2017.

"There are principles worth defending, even if they come at a cost. And this one, for me, is one of them.

- Man City chairman on club's Premier League charges case: 'Nothing has changed'

"Now, almost nine years after those words at Soccerex, an independent Premier League commission has deemed 114 of the 115 financial breaches charged against Manchester City proven, according to the published reports.

"There's still a way to go. The sanction remains to be known, and the process isn't over. But what's happened once again shows why economic control, transparency, and equal rules for all are essential to protect the integrity and sustainability of football."

"We will keep defending those principles. Just like in 2017."

Information from PA contributed to this story.
